text: AI-powered cultural archive for India's architectural memory
A working system for digitization, OCR, search, maps and source-grounded research
HackCult '26, Problem Statement 2. The working prototype claim is supported by the deployed frontend and automated test suite. Image source is recorded in frontend/public/images/sites/ATTRIBUTION.md.
The problem and what the system must achieve
Heritage evidence exists, but its formats and archives cannot work together.
Photographs lack metadata. Scanned documents hide their text. Field notes and regional records remain disconnected from the monuments they describe.
Durable private storage and authorized downloads
PDF extraction and OCR for scanned sources
Sites, documents, images and map coordinates
Open browsing, filtering and grounded answers
Problem and requirements come from the hackathon brief and the implemented HeritageLens workflow. No size, accuracy or adoption claims are made.
HeritageLens turns scattered sources into a usable archive
The judges can inspect the deployed product, not a mock-up.
Site metadata plus extracted and corrected document text
PDF extraction, Tesseract OCR and curator correction
Coordinates connect monuments to archival records
Screenshot captured from https://heritage-pearl.vercel.app/. Features are verified in frontend routes, backend services and automated tests.
From an uploaded source to verified discovery
Automation handles repetitive processing. Curators retain editorial control.
The backend records errors, preserves the original source and can resubmit interrupted background work after restart.
Workflow verified in backend document router, storage service and background processing service. Upload polling and curator review are implemented in the frontend UploadPage.
The repository uses one modular backend with clear boundaries for storage, processing and public discovery.

The current system can support a controlled institutional pilot. Each feasibility claim has evidence and a defined next step.

Ready for a controlled pilot. A broader rollout still needs individual curator roles, production monitoring and a managed job queue.

Feasibility is framed for a controlled pilot rather than a full institutional rollout. The architecture and repository support each current-build claim. Live Supabase storage and production migrations still require deployment verification. Cost claims are qualitative because production usage data is not available.
The current product solves preservation and discovery first. Phase 2 can improve multilingual retrieval after production verification.

HeritageLens makes cultural evidence searchable without losing the path back to its source.
The roadmap clearly separates implemented functionality from future work. Phase 2 multilingual semantic retrieval has not been implemented.
